title: The Fork on the Table
content:
When Daniel arrived at the old hotel, it was already dark. He had booked a room for one night because he was traveling through a small town and needed a place to sleep.

The hotel was almost empty. An old receptionist gave him a key and pointed toward the stairs.

— Your room is on the second floor. Breakfast is served at seven.

— Thank you.

Daniel went upstairs and entered his room. Everything looked clean, but something felt strangely uncomfortable. On the small table beside the window, there was a single fork.

He hadn't noticed it when he entered.

Daniel picked it up and placed it in the drawer. Then he went to bed.

Around midnight, he woke up because he heard a noise in the hallway. Someone was walking slowly outside his room.

He got up and opened the door.

Nobody was there.

However, the fork was back on the table.

Daniel stared at it for several seconds.

— That's impossible.

He put it back in the drawer and locked the door.

The next morning, he went downstairs for breakfast. The receptionist was sitting behind the desk.

— Did you sleep well? — she asked.

— Not really. Something strange happened in my room.

The receptionist looked worried.

— What happened?

— I found a fork on the table twice. I put it in the drawer, but it came back.

The woman's expression suddenly changed.

— Which room are you staying in?

— Room 207.

She became silent.

— If I had known you were staying there, I would have given you another room.

Daniel felt a chill.

— Why?

The receptionist looked toward the stairs.

— A guest stayed in that room many years ago. He disappeared during the night. Nobody ever found out what happened to him.

Daniel remembered the fork.

— What does the fork have to do with him?

— I don't know. But according to the old stories, he always ate dinner alone in that room.

Daniel immediately returned upstairs to collect his things. When he opened the door, the fork was lying on the bed.

He picked it up and noticed something engraved on the handle: a date and a name.

Thomas Reed — October 14, 1978.

Daniel took a photograph of it and showed it to the receptionist.

She recognized the name immediately.

— That's the guest who disappeared.

Daniel looked at the fork again.

— If you had told me about this last night, I wouldn't have stayed in that room.

The receptionist lowered her eyes.

— I'm sorry.

Daniel left the hotel as quickly as possible.

Years later, he still remembered that strange night. Sometimes he wondered what would have happened if he hadn't found the fork, or if he hadn't opened the door when he heard the footsteps.

Perhaps he would have forgotten the hotel completely.

But he had found the fork.

And someone—or something—had wanted him to find it.
